findings.issue: The BUILD rule replaces the issue's joint median >=40% improvement, >=4/5 next-class preference, and no-child-PII requirements with time <50% alone. Its NARROW/REJECT branches overlap and leave intermediate results undecided. Restore the issue's BUILD/SIMPLIFY/DO NOT BUILD contract with an explicit fallback.

The protocol omits willingness-to-pay/repeated-use evidence required by #3, although low intent is used in the decision rule. Add concrete interview and recording instructions without extrapolating market size.

Privacy/copyright/support implications are only a placeholder and authorization is absent. The proposed distribution model does not define per-project management capabilities, read-only family scope, source sharing restrictions, or required PDF license notices.

The study method only schedules 10 learners and timing; it omits the specified 20/30-learner and last-minute level-change tasks and a common error-counting method for the current flow and both prototypes.

summary: Corrected all four research-plan defects: decision gates, demand evidence, authorization/licensing boundaries, and observation tasks; four regressions were red before the fix and all 21 related tests now pass. Full suite: 821 passed, one existing worktree-hook check failed, coverage 96.99%; ruff and mypy passed. needs-human: recruitment and observations with at least five real teachers remain outstanding, so this plan cannot close issue #3.
